questions.q: Why does profiles.yml never get committed to the dbt project's git repository?
options: It holds real connection details, including a password or key, for each developer — a secret that should never end up in version control
git does not support YAML files
dbt automatically deletes profiles.yml after every build
profiles.yml is auto-generated and therefore not worth tracking
questions.explain: profiles.yml lives at ~/.dbt/profiles.yml, outside any folder pushed to the repo, specifically because it carries real credentials.

questions.q: Why does this lesson's profile set target: dev as the default?
options: Because prod doesn't exist until Chapter 6
So plain dbt build with no --target flag builds into the safe dev schema by default, requiring a deliberate --target prod to touch production directly
Because dev is the only target dbt supports without extra configuration
Because Snowflake requires dev to be listed first alphabetically
questions.explain: Making dev the default target is a deliberate safety choice — touching prod by hand requires an explicit, intentional flag.

questions.q: What does every sensitive value in this lesson's profiles.yml use instead of a literal string?
options: A hardcoded password visible in plain text
env_var(...), dbt's Jinja function for reading a value from an environment variable at run time
A Python f-string
A separate .env file referenced by relative path inside profiles.yml
questions.explain: env_var(...) keeps nothing sensitive written as literal text in the file — the same pattern Lesson 20's CI-generated profiles.yml reuses.

questions.q: Why might a real team set each developer's dev target schema to dev_alice or dev_bob instead of a single shared dev schema?
options: So two developers building at the same time never step on each other's half-finished models — each gets an isolated personal schema
Because dbt requires a unique schema name per machine
Because Snowflake limits one schema to one query at a time
It has no real benefit; it's purely a naming convention
questions.explain: A personal dev schema per developer is the real-world fix for the collision risk named back in Lesson 5.

questions.q: What does running dbt debug confirm?
options: That every dbt test in the project currently passes
That the account, user, role, warehouse, and database in profiles.yml all resolve and that dbt can actually connect
That the GitHub Actions workflow is correctly configured
That every model's SQL is syntactically valid
questions.explain: dbt debug is specifically a connection check — the right first command to run after writing or editing profiles.yml, before building anything.
